about: A fictional web shop's memory after a few weeks of agent sessions. Queries are written the way people ask, often without the memory's exact words. 'expect' lists the memories a good answer needs; an empty list means the prompt names no topic and nothing should be injected.

memories.text: Stripe webhooks must be verified against the raw request body; the JSON body parser breaks the signature check.
Local Stripe testing uses stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/webhooks/stripe and the sk_test key from .env.example.
Refunds must send an Idempotency-Key header; retries without it double-refund customers.
Prices are stored in minor units (cents) as integers. Never use floats for money.
Sales tax is calculated by TaxJar at checkout, not in our code; we cache rates for 24 hours.
Guest carts expire after 7 days and are deleted by the nightly cleanup job.
Inventory is reserved with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the order transaction to stop overselling.
Order states: pending -> paid -> packed -> shipped -> delivered; cancelled is only allowed before packed.
Shipping rates come from the Shippo API; free shipping applies above 75 USD after discounts.
Transactional email goes through Postmark; templates live in emails/ and are previewed with npm run email:dev.
Login uses httpOnly session cookies stored in Redis with a 14 day sliding expiry; there are no JWTs.
The login endpoint is rate limited to 5 attempts per minute per IP and per email.
Password reset tokens are single use and expire after 30 minutes; the link must use APP_URL, not the request host.
Admin roles are owner, manager and support; only owner can issue refunds above 500 USD.
Database migrations use Prisma: npx prisma migrate dev locally, migrate deploy in CI. Never edit an applied migration.
Seed local data with npm run db:seed; it creates 40 products and the test admin user.
Product search is Meilisearch; the index is rebuilt by npm run search:reindex after bulk imports.
Product images are stored in S3 and served through CloudFront with on-the-fly resizing via ?w= parameters.
Feature flags are read from LaunchDarkly; local development falls back to flags.local.json.
End-to-end tests use Playwright: npm run test:e2e starts the app on port 3100 and needs the seeded database.
Unit tests run with Vitest (npm test); snapshot files live next to the components.
checkout.spec.ts is flaky when Stripe test mode is slow; it waits for the payment-intent webhook, not a fixed timeout.
The storefront deploys to Vercel on merge to main; preview deployments are created for every pull request.
Background jobs run on a separate Fly.io worker app deployed with fly deploy -c fly.worker.toml.
Secrets are managed in Doppler; never commit .env files. New variables must be added to .env.example.
Jobs use BullMQ on Redis; failed jobs retry 5 times with exponential backoff, then land in the dead-letter queue.
The store is translated into English, German and French with next-intl; message files are in messages/*.json.
We use PostHog for product analytics and turned off session recording on checkout pages for privacy.
Coupons do not stack: only the single best discount is applied, and gift cards are applied after discounts.
Dana owns payments and refunds; ask her before changing anything under src/payments.
Luis maintains search and the product catalog import.
UI uses Tailwind with the design tokens in tailwind.config.ts; do not add new hex colors inline.
Every interactive element needs a visible focus ring and an accessible name; axe runs in the e2e suite.
Product pages must stay under 170 KB of JavaScript; the bundle check fails CI above that.
Fixed a tax rounding bug where totals were off by one cent for multi-item orders; rounding now happens once on the order total.
After the October Redis outage, sessions fail open to read-only browsing instead of logging everyone out.
